title: CLSI/EUCAST structured standards engine
text: Breakpoints and interpretive rules must be represented as a licensed, version-controlled structured database. CLSI and EUCAST update rules and QC information; EUCAST publishes current clinical and RAST-specific tables, while CLSI emphasizes use of current standards and method-specific procedures [S12-S14].
tables: Organism/group, antimicrobial, method, specimen/workflow where relevant
Medium, inoculum, incubation, atmosphere, reading time, disk content or MIC panel
S/I/R thresholds, ATU/uncertainty areas, non-reportable combinations and exceptions
Reference strains, acceptable ranges, frequency and lot controls
Publisher, document/version, effective dates, licensed source and change record
Deterministic rule result plus human-readable explanation and exact applied rule

NON-NEGOTIABLE CORRECTION
An LLM or RAG system may retrieve and explain approved guidance, but it must not invent, infer or silently update clinical breakpoints. RAST results must use the matching RAST method, organism, antimicrobial and reading-time table - not standard overnight breakpoints [S13].
